title: Unpatterned Wafer Inspection - Micro-cracks Detection on Puma 9900
subtitle: Final Inspection Quality Validation for 45nm Node Manufacturing
author: Emily Nakamura

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Puma 9900 system to detect and classify Micro-cracks defects during final inspection inspection at the 45nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Micro-cracks defects that are critical to yield at the 45nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Puma 9900 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Puma 9900
- Inspection Type: Unpatterned Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: Micro-cracks
- Process Step: Final Inspection
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 45nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all Puma 9900 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for final inspection monitoring in the 45nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Puma 9900
Software Version: v8.3.139
Recipe: UNPATTERNED_WAFER_INSPECTION_45nm_FINAL INSPECTION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (98 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Puma 9900 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Unpatterned Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Micro-cracks defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 45nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 83 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 93% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.7% for Unpatterned Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.97 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-01-30
Wafers Tested: 21
Total Defects Found: 4473
Defect Density: 632.8 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 2.9%
Capture Rate: 97.6%
Test Duration: 100 minutes
System Uptime: 98.4%

Result Classification: NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Puma 9900 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Micro-cracks at the 45nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
